description: Ground-truth classification of the nursery's 'generated-mutation' rows in the train/development partitions. Every row here is FALSE, established by a concrete counterexample rather than by looking at the mutation label. This is the negative-control population a producer census is checked against by scripts/check-autogenesis-must-decline-population.py: a census that reports any one of these fact_ids as an admitted/admissible proof is void, because admitting a false statement is a soundness failure, not a low conversion rate.
population_definition: every entry with provenance_class == 'generated-mutation' and partition != 'held-out'
held_out_exclusion: 2 of the nursery's 12 generated-mutation rows are partition 'held-out' (natural-square-root and natural-binomial families) and are deliberately NOT evaluated or referenced here, by name or fact_id, per the held-out isolation policy in scripts/check-autogenesis-holdout-isolation.py. Determining ground truth for a held-out row and publishing that determination in a committed artifact is itself a form of touching the partition; it is withheld the same way an operation's fact_ids over held-out are withheld. AMENDED 2026-08-30: this said 3 rows and named natural-logarithm among them. The ADR-0542 amendment moved that family out of held-out, which correctly brought its mutation row into the must-decline population and left this artifact stale -- the gate caught it, naming exactly the one row and NOT the square-root row that is still blind.
verification_method: Each row's witness is a concrete Nat/Int numeral (or tuple of numerals) that a bounded, elementary evaluator (embedded in scripts/check-autogenesis-must-decline-population.py) recomputes independently at gate time -- the JSON below is not trusted on its own; check_kind selects the evaluator function and the gate refuses to pass if recomputation does not confirm the refutation. Every witness is small enough to check by hand.

entries.counterexample_explanation: Nat.fib 1 = 1, so the left side (fib n = 0) is false at n = 1, but the widened right side (n = 0 ∨ n = 1) is true at n = 1. A biconditional with one side true and the other false is false.

entries.formal_statement: ∀ {x y : ℤ}, x.gcd y ≠ 0 → x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0
entries.counterexample_explanation: gcd(0, 5) = 5 ≠ 0, so the hypothesis holds, but x = 0 makes the strengthened conjunctive conclusion (x ≠ 0 ∧ y ≠ 0) false. (The original, un-mutated statement uses ∨ here, which this witness leaves true.)
p = 2 is prime, so the hypothesis holds. p.pred = 1, and the strengthened conclusion needs 1 < p.pred, i.e. 1 < 1, which is false. (The original statement only needed 0 < p.pred, which 1 satisfies.)
0! = 1 by the standard empty-product convention, so n.factorial = 0 fails at n = 0. (n.factorial != 0 for every n, so any n witnesses this; n = 0 is the smallest.)

1 ||| 0 (bitwise OR) = 1, and 1 &&& 0 (bitwise AND) = 0. 1 ≠ 0, so the substituted-operator equality fails. (The original statement compares n ||| m to m ||| n, i.e. commutativity of OR, which this witness does not bear on.)

For nonnegative n, Int.fib n = Nat.fib n (the standard extension only changes the sign convention for negative n), so at n = 1 this is the same failure as the Nat.fib mutation: fib(1) = 1 ≠ 0 while n = 1 makes the widened right side true.

entries.formal_statement: ∀ {n a b : ℤ}, b ≡ a [ZMOD n]
entries.counterexample_explanation: The premise 'a ≡ b [ZMOD n]' was removed, leaving an unconditional claim that ALL a, b are congruent mod every n. At n = 2, a = 0, b = 1: a % n = 0 and b % n = 1, which differ, so b ≡ a [ZMOD 2] is false.

Nat.Coprime a b is defined as gcd a b = 1. gcd(0, 0) = 0 by the standard convention (gcd 0 n = n), and 0 ≠ 1, so Nat.Coprime 0 0 is false. (The un-mutated original states the negation, ¬Nat.Coprime 0 0, which this same fact confirms.)

entries.formal_statement: ∀ {n a b : ℕ}, b ≡ a [MOD n]
entries.counterexample_explanation: Same shape as the Int.ModEq.symm mutation, over ℕ instead of ℤ: the premise was removed, and at n = 2, a = 0, b = 1, a % n = 0 while b % n = 1, so b ≡ a [MOD 2] is false.

entries.formal_statement: ∀ (b x : ℕ), Nat.log b x < x
entries.counterexample_explanation: Nat.log b 0 = 0 for every b (the definition returns 0 when n < b, and 0 < b for any b >= 1; for b <= 1 it returns 0 outright). So the conclusion reads 0 < 0, which is false. The parent F:ml430-nat-log-le-self states Nat.log b n <= n, which holds at n = 0 as 0 <= 0 -- strengthening <= to < is exactly what breaks it.
0 choose 0 is 1: selecting no elements from the empty set has exactly one witness, the empty selection. Therefore the claimed equality to 0 fails already at n = 0.

independent_audit.method: each witness recomputed from scratch in plain Python using the language's own math.factorial / math.gcd / % / | / &, independently of the derivation that produced this file
independent_audit.positive_control: 13 known-answer cases (factorial 0 and 5, choose 0 0, descFactorial 5 1, ascFactorial 1 3, fib 10, gcd 0 0, gcd 0 5, pred 2, 1|0, 1&0, 0%2, 1%2) all matched their expected values
independent_audit.negative_control: the TRUE statement forall n, descFactorial n 0 = 1 yields zero counterexamples over n < 20 -- a method that refutes everything would prove nothing
independent_audit.hypothesis_check: two entries are implications whose witness must SATISFY the hypothesis before the conclusion can refute anything -- gcd(0,5) != 0 holds, and Prime 2 holds -- and both were confirmed rather than assumed
